sealed.statement: The ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner semantic generation for a node is a pure function of that node's OWN observed semantic inputs S(N) = {dimensions, runtimeAuthority, priorityControlPlaneRecovery, runtimeServeEligible, nodeEvidence, membershipPublication} — every field canonically digested with observation-time fields excluded (membershipPublication via a digest cached per frozen diagnostics object, its top-level createdAt/updatedAt classified observation-time) — and carries NO cluster-wide version segment and NO planning-derivation segment, so an authoritative mutation rotates node N's generation if and only if it changes N's observed semantic inputs. Invariants: (DEP-SCOPE) every field reaching the owner seam is classified with a source-owner justification and the seam fails CLOSED (build without memoizing, counted) for any unclassified field or digest depth overflow; (A1) a mutation proven to affect only node A rotates A while B returns the SAME core reference without normalizing again; (A2) A observes the new semantic result — no stale node-local entry; (A3) a membership-publication content change (epoch/status/ack lists) rotates every node's generation, while a CONTROL_PLANE_PUBLICATIONS write that leaves the membership diagnostics' semantic content unchanged rotates no node; (A4) a mutation affecting a bounded node subset rebuilds exactly that subset; (A5) live transport/lifecycle/publication-mode/repair changes rotate exactly as v2 DEP and v4 established, raw nodeEvidence transport fields included; (A6) a publication change arriving while a graph is being built, or between a cache apply and its deferred listener on the sync path, never publishes old evidence under a newer generation, on the REAL SystemTableCache; (PLANNING) a planning-derivation tick that changes no verdict leaves every core reused by reference and a planning change that flips a verdict still rotates through the digested verdict; (ENGAGEMENT) under production-shaped churn (five nodes, moving clock, writes repeatedly concerning one/some nodes, planning latch live) unaffected nodes' cores actually reuse, and the receipt reds when either the six cluster-wide table versions or the planning segment is restored to the key; (BOUNDED-WORK) builds(N) <= changes to S(N) + 1 initial build — never cluster table writes x node count; (LIVE) on the local docker formation fixture (LAGRANGE_LOOP_GAP_PROFILE=1 npm run demo:movielens, seed node, formation window) owner reuse is >= 50% with builds per sync read <= 0.35, against 8.8% and 0.55 measured before. The generation uses no TTL, clock, evaluation count or object identity as an invalidation signal (a WeakMap digest cache on frozen objects is a pure cache). Scope owns ONLY the generation of the ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner and the sync publication-diagnostics memo keying; it does NOT own the planning latch itself, OwnerKeyReconcileQueue cadence, ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner loop frequency, trust-state/dispatch caller frequency, candidate-derivation self-cost, storage_reservation_reconcile, or schema admission.

hypothesis: Make the ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner generation a pure content digest of the node's own observed semantic inputs: membershipPublication digested with a per-frozen-object digest cache (top-level createdAt/updatedAt observation-time), nodeEvidence digested (heartbeatAgeMs/readyLeaseAgeMs observation-time), no cluster-wide table version and no planning segment in the key; typed COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE generation with fail-closed unowned builds (unclassified seam field, digest overflow); per-cause build attribution (sync sections + stats + per-node stats); sync publication-diagnostics memo stamped with the synchronous table version; dead version-bracket threading removed from the node methods; receipts DEP-SCOPE/A1-A6/A3b/PLANNING/ENGAGEMENT/BOUNDED-WORK/LIVE

claim: independent landing verification rejected (subagent-per-node-generation-v2-review-1): adversarial-js-intrinsics: F1 (blocking): the sealed DEP-SCOPE fail-closed invariant does not hold on the overflow branch. In src/control-plane/projection-readiness-evidence-generation.js canonicalScalarDigest renders a container at the depth cap as DIGEST_TAG.OPAQUE_PREFIX + String(value); String() throws TypeError (Cannot convert object to primitive value) for a null-prototype container and invokes user toString/Symbol.toPrimitive for any object, so buildProjectionReadinessGeneration throws out of buildDimensionsEvaluation instead of returning INCOMPLETE digest_depth_overflow. Reproduce: let deep = Object.create(null); deep.leaf = true; for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) deep = {deep}; buildProjectionReadinessGeneration({...base, runtimeAuthority: deep}, classifiedSource) -> TypeError, while the same nesting of plain objects -> {state: incomplete, reason: digest_depth_overflow}. Null-prototype records are routine inside the digested graphs (membership-publication-priority-partition-summary.js exclusionReasonCounts, canonical-data copies, every copyStrictOwnDataRecord output), today at depth <= 3, so current shapes do not reach it; the invariant exists for the shapes that are not current. Fix: emit a constant opaque token (no coercion) for the overflow branch and a typeof tag for non-object non-primitives, keeping trace.overflow = true.; adversarial-js-intrinsics: F2 (address or justify): the canonical digest is not injective over the strict normalizer's input domain, so the shape-independent claim 'rotates iff N's observed semantic inputs change' is carried only by today's fixed record schemas. (ii) Values the normalizer rejects whole-source (Date, class instance, symbol or non-enumerable key, accessor, sparse array) digest identically to their plain twins while buildProjectionReadinessContract flips between a valid core and the degenerate sourceInvalid core -> same key, different core (probe script in the verdict narrative). Not reachable with service-built records; the corrective attempt should either length-prefix strings/keys and mark the generation INCOMPLETE for any visited value that copyStrictOwnDataRecord/copyDenseOwnDataArray would reject (non-plain prototype, non-data or symbol key, hole), or document in the module why the digest domain may be wider than the normalizer domain.; harness-fidelity: F3 (recommendation, address or justify): the DEP-SCOPE depth receipt pins record depths 1/2/5/1/1/5 against DIGEST_MAX_DEPTH 8 on an idle five-node fixture with no in-flight priority recovery. The normalizer already bounds depth at PROJECTION_READINESS_MAX_OWN_DATA_DEPTH 16, so raising the digest cap to match removes the cliff at no soundness cost (cycles still overflow); the receipt should measure depth on a fixture carrying witness content or state the margin explicitly. findings.summary: F1 (blocking): the sealed DEP-SCOPE fail-closed invariant does not hold on the overflow branch. In src/control-plane/projection-readiness-evidence-generation.js canonicalScalarDigest renders a container at the depth cap as DIGEST_TAG.OPAQUE_PREFIX + String(value); String() throws TypeError (Cannot convert object to primitive value) for a null-prototype container and invokes user toString/Symbol.toPrimitive for any object, so buildProjectionReadinessGeneration throws out of buildDimensionsEvaluation instead of returning INCOMPLETE digest_depth_overflow. Reproduce: let deep = Object.create(null); deep.leaf = true; for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) deep = {deep}; buildProjectionReadinessGeneration({...base, runtimeAuthority: deep}, classifiedSource) -> TypeError, while the same nesting of plain objects -> {state: incomplete, reason: digest_depth_overflow}. Null-prototype records are routine inside the digested graphs (membership-publication-priority-partition-summary.js exclusionReasonCounts, canonical-data copies, every copyStrictOwnDataRecord output), today at depth <= 3, so current shapes do not reach it; the invariant exists for the shapes that are not current. Fix: emit a constant opaque token (no coercion) for the overflow branch and a typeof tag for non-object non-primitives, keeping trace.overflow = true.

F2 (address or justify): the canonical digest is not injective over the strict normalizer's input domain, so the shape-independent claim 'rotates iff N's observed semantic inputs change' is carried only by today's fixed record schemas. (i) String leaves and keys are concatenated unescaped and without a length prefix: {a:'x', b:'y'} and {a:'x;b=s:y'} digest identically, as do ['a','b'] and ['a,s:b']. (ii) Values the normalizer rejects whole-source (Date, class instance, symbol or non-enumerable key, accessor, sparse array) digest identically to their plain twins while buildProjectionReadinessContract flips between a valid core and the degenerate sourceInvalid core -> same key, different core (probe script in the verdict narrative). Not reachable with service-built records; the corrective attempt should either length-prefix strings/keys and mark the generation INCOMPLETE for any visited value that copyStrictOwnDataRecord/copyDenseOwnDataArray would reject (non-plain prototype, non-data or symbol key, hole), or document in the module why the digest domain may be wider than the normalizer domain.

F3 (recommendation, address or justify): the DEP-SCOPE depth receipt pins record depths 1/2/5/1/1/5 against DIGEST_MAX_DEPTH 8 on an idle five-node fixture with no in-flight priority recovery. Under live recovery priorityControlPlaneRecovery.priorityRecoveryObservation.priorityRecoveryCurrentSummary.partitionSnapshots[i].operationOwnerObservation / topologyOperatorWitness records (priority-recovery-observation-partition-witness.js) reach depth 6-7, leaving one or two levels of headroom; an overflow is fail-closed and counted so soundness holds, but the memo would silently switch off in the recovery window the quest targets. The normalizer already bounds depth at PROJECTION_READINESS_MAX_OWN_DATA_DEPTH 16, so raising the digest cap to match removes the cliff at no soundness cost (cycles still overflow); the receipt should measure depth on a fixture carrying witness content or state the margin explicitly. The archived live run recorded 0 unowned builds.

control-plane-readiness-stored-snapshot-reuse.js getFresherStoredReadinessSnapshot overrides the top-level membershipPublication with the fresh diagnostics while keeping the stored core and dimensions. Before this candidate the sync memo was equally stale in the macrotask between a publication apply and its listener, so both halves were consistently old; with the version-stamped memo that window becomes mixed-freshness (top-level at the new epoch, core at the old epoch) until the deferred listener invalidates. Already recorded by the author as a separate owner; the candidate changes the shape of the window rather than introducing it.

ProjectionReadinessEvidenceOwner.statsByNodeId is created for every nodeId that reaches resolveContract and is never pruned, and entryByNodeId is never pruned in production because invalidateNode has no src caller. Node ids are per-boot UUIDs, so a long-lived seed accumulates one small record per join/rejoin. Pre-existing for entryByNodeId; statsByNodeId is new in this candidate.

The comment block above GENERATION_TABLE_VERSION_KV in projection-readiness-evidence-generation.js still says the membershipPublication graph is 'covered by the global table version instead', which the candidate no longer does, and the dep-scope map section 6 names the fail-closed reason unclassified_source_skip while the code emits unclassified_source_field.

test/shards/primary-classes.json, resource-classes.json and subsystem-classes.json are modified in the worktree (census entries for the new receipt file) but are not in the review manifest's candidate paths; the two previous quest landings (50bfe369b, c81554f14) committed those census files together with test/shards/impact-graph-seal.json, which is not regenerated here. The landing should carry them or the audit:shards check will flag drift.

The archived after-v2 seed log has four 'Initial table partition provisioning failed: Unable to satisfy minimum routable provisioning cohort ... provisionable=0' errors at 55-80 s that the BEFORE run lacks (the v1 run has eight). The node trust states at those instants (planning_snapshot_refresh_pending, transport_unknown, freshness_unknown, later PRIORITY_CONTROL_PLANE_RECOVERY_PENDING) are the same class BEFORE shows at 19:34:22-24; the difference is that BEFORE's retries found an existing routable replica on the seed and v2's did not. Not attributable to the key from the logs (those trust states are envelope-derived), but the LIVE receipt's 'same downstream family' wording covers only the ratings failure and the v2 run ended at 5.5 min versus 16 min for BEFORE. The seed and joiner counters re-extract exactly as claimed (85,163 -> 69,960 sync reads, 47,402 -> 7,627 builds, 8.6% -> 81.4% reuse, 0 unowned; joiners 74/79/81/65%).

Readiness services that hold the read-only cache proxy (src/cache/read-only-system-table-cache.js exposes getAll and onCacheChange but not getTableMutationVersion) receive the constant memo stamp and keep the deferred-listener window on the sync diagnostics memo; the A6 repair therefore covers only caches with a version surface. Pre-existing CL-019 behavior, unchanged by the candidate, and the content key is sound there regardless (it also removes the v3/v4 latent under-invalidation on joiners that the v1 measurement recorded).

hypothesis: Corrective attempt for review-0f76ab4e: (F1) overflow and non-object leaves render constant tokens with no coercion, so a null-prototype or hostile-toString container at the cap fails CLOSED instead of throwing; (F2) the digest mirrors the strict own-data normalizer's domain — plain/null prototypes, string enumerable data keys, dense canonical arrays, no proxies/function/symbol leaves — with a new digest_domain_violation INCOMPLETE reason, and strings/keys are length-prefixed for injectivity; (F3) the digest cap is the normalizer's PROJECTION_READINESS_MAX_OWN_DATA_DEPTH (16, now exported); receipts for each; dep-scope doc updated
